babs.0: How the revelation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began

1.matn: Al-Humaydi ʿAbd Allah ibn az-Zubayr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim at-Taymi reported to me that he heard ʿAlqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, on the pulpit. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Actions are only by intentions, and each person has only what he intended. So whoever emigrated for a worldly gain he seeks, or for a woman he wishes to marry, his emigration is for what he emigrated to.”
1.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the intention decides what the deed counts for. In Fath al-Bari, Ibn Hajar explains that the intention is in the heart and that emigration here is an example for every deed. In this narration via al-Ḥumaydī the sentence about emigrating for Allah and His Messenger does not occur; this is how al-Bukhārī transmits it here. It does occur in other narrations in al-Bukhārī, for example no. 54 and no. 6689.

2.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us: Mālik informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her: Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, may Allah be pleased with him, asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “O Messenger of Allah, how does the revelation come to you?” He said: “Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me. Then it leaves me, and I have retained what was said. And sometimes the angel appears to me in the form of a man; he speaks to me and I retain what he says.” ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I saw the revelation descending upon him on an extremely cold day; then it left him, and his forehead was dripping with sweat.
2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the report distinguishes two ways in which revelation came, the heavy coming like the ringing of a bell and the angel speaking in human form. The sweat on his forehead is ʿĀʾisha’s own observation, may Allah be pleased with her, and not an embellishment.

3.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa ibn az-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, that she said: The first of the revelation with which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was begun was the true dream in sleep. He would not see a dream except that it came like the brightness of dawn. Then seclusion was made dear to him. He would withdraw to the cave of Ḥirāʾ and devote himself to worship there for a number of nights before returning to his family, and he would take provisions for that. Then he would return to Khadīja and take provisions for a similar stay, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Ḥirāʾ. The angel came to him and said: “Read!” He said: “I am not one who reads.” He said: He took hold of me and pressed me until it exhausted me, then released me and said: “Read!” I said: “I am not one who reads.” He took hold of me a second time and pressed me until it exhausted me, then released me and said: “Read!” I said: “I am not one who reads.” He took hold of me a third time and pressed me, then released me and said: “Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned with it, his heart trembling. He came in to Khadīja bint Khuwaylid, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: “Wrap me up, wrap me up.” They wrapped him until the fear left him. Then he told Khadīja what had happened and said: “I feared for myself.” Khadīja said: “No, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep the ties of kinship, you bear the burden of the weak, you earn for the destitute, you honour the guest, and you help against the misfortunes that befall the truth.” Then Khadīja went with him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, Khadīja’s cousin. He had become a Christian in the time before Islam. He used to write the Hebrew script and would write from the Gospel in Hebrew as much as Allah willed him to write. He was a very old man who had become blind. Khadīja said to him: “O my cousin, listen to the son of your brother.” Waraqa said to him: “O son of my brother, what do you see?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told him what he had seen. Waraqa said to him: “This is the Nāmūs whom Allah sent down upon Mūsā. Would that I were young then! Would that I were alive when your people drive you out!” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Will they drive me out?” He said: “Yes. No man has ever brought the like of what you have brought except that he was met with hostility. If your day reaches me, I will support you with strong support.” Then it was not long before Waraqa died, and the revelation paused for a time.
3.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the report narrates the beginning of revelation, the first verses of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, and the words of Khadīja and Waraqa. It is a narrative, not an invented commentary from Fatḥ al-Bārī with a page number.

4.matn: Ibn Shihāb said: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān informed me that Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Anṣārī said, while speaking about the pause in revelation: “While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze, and there was the angel who had come to me at Ḥirāʾ, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was frightened of him, so I returned and said: Wrap me up. Then Allah, the Exalted, sent down: O you who are wrapped, arise and warn, up to His words: and shun impurity. Then the revelation became intense and continued in succession.” ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf and Abū Ṣāliḥ followed him in this. Hilāl ibn Raddād followed him from az-Zuhrī. Yūnus and Maʿmar said: “his trembling muscles”.
4.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the report continues the account of the pause in revelation and names the opening verses of Sūrat al-Muddaththir. The final sentences are supporting chains and wording variants, not a new statement of their own.

5.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us: Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha narrated to us: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bear great strain when revelation came down, and he would move his lips. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I move them for you as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to move them. Saʿīd said: I move them as I saw Ibn ʿAbbās move them, and he moved his lips. So Allah, the Exalted, sent down: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Upon Us is its gathering and its recitation.” He said: Its gathering in your chest, and that you recite it. “So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.” He said: Listen to it and be silent. “Then upon Us is its explanation.” Then upon Us is that you recite it. After that, when Jibrīl came to him, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would listen; and when Jibrīl left, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would recite it as he had recited it.
5.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the verses about the tongue. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, first listened and then recited. No page number from a commentary is invented.

6.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh informed us: Yūnus informed us, from az-Zuhrī. And Bishr ibn Muḥammad narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh informed us: Yūnus and Maʿmar informed us, from az-Zuhrī, with similar wording. He said: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramaḍān when Jibrīl met him. Jibrīl would meet him every night of Ramaḍān and study the Qurʾān with him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was then more generous with good than the wind that is sent forth.
6.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the report describes the generosity of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and how it increased in Ramaḍān while he went through the Qurʾān with Jibrīl. No page number is invented.

7.matn: Abū l-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us: Shuʿayb informed us, from az-Zuhrī: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd informed me that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him that Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb informed him: Heraclius sent for him while he was with a caravan of Quraysh. They were merchants in Shām during the period in which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had made a truce with Abū Sufyān and the disbelievers of Quraysh. They came to him while they were in Īliyāʾ. He called them into his court, and around him were the great men of the Romans. Then he called them, and called his interpreter, and said: “Which of you is closest in kinship to this man who claims to be a prophet?” Abū Sufyān said: I said: “I am the closest of them to him in kinship.” He said: “Bring him near to me, and bring his companions near and place them behind his back.” Then he said to his interpreter: “Tell them that I will question this man about him. If he lies to me, contradict him.” Abū Sufyān said: By Allah, had it not been for the shame of their passing on a lie from me, I would have lied about him. The first thing he asked me about him was: “What is his lineage among you?” I said: “He is of noble lineage among us.” He said: “Has anyone among you ever said this word before him?” I said: “No.” He said: “Was any of his forefathers a king?” I said: “No.” He said: “Do the nobles among the people follow him, or the weak?” I said: “Rather the weak.” He said: “Are they increasing or decreasing?” I said: “They are increasing.” He said: “Does any of them turn away out of displeasure with his religion after entering it?” I said: “No.” He said: “Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?” I said: “No.” He said: “Does he betray?” I said: “No. And we are now in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do in it.” Abū Sufyān said: I found no other word in which I could insert something except this one. He said: “Have you fought him?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “And how was your fighting with him?” I said: “War between us and him goes back and forth: he gains from us and we gain from him.” He said: “What does he command you?” I said: “He says: Worship Allah alone and associate nothing with Him, and abandon what your forefathers say. And he commands us to pray, to be truthful, to be chaste and to keep the ties of kinship.” Then he said to the interpreter: “Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you said that he is of noble lineage among you. Thus are messengers sent from the noble lineage of their people. I asked you whether anyone among you had said this word before, and you said no. Had anyone said it before him, I would have said: a man imitating a word said before him. I asked you whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you said no. Had one of his forefathers been a king, I would have said: a man seeking his father’s kingdom. I asked you whether you accused him of lying before he said what he said, and you said no. I knew that he would not refrain from lying to people and then lie about Allah. I asked you whether the nobles followed him or the weak, and you said that the weak followed him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked you whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you said they are increasing. Such is the matter of faith until it is complete. I asked you whether anyone turns away out of displeasure with his religion after entering it, and you said no. Such is faith when its joy mingles with the hearts. I asked you whether he betrays, and you said no. Thus messengers do not betray. I asked you what he commands you, and you said that he commands you to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, that he forbids you the worship of idols, and that he commands you to pray, to be truthful and to be chaste. If what you say is true, he will possess the place of these two feet of mine. I knew that he was going to appear, but I did not think that he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would take the trouble to meet him; and if I were with him, I would wash his feet.” Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which he had sent with Diḥya to the governor of Buṣrā, who passed it to Heraclius. He read it, and in it was: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy. From Muḥammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe, and Allah will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the common people. “O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equal between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take one another as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.” Abū Sufyān said: When he had said what he said and finished reading the letter, there was a great clamour around him, voices were raised, and we were taken out. I said to my companions when we were taken out: “The matter of the son of Abū Kabsha has grown great. Even the king of the Banū l-Aṣfar fears him.” I remained certain that he would prevail, until Allah brought Islam into my heart. Ibn an-Nāṭūr, the governor of Īliyāʾ and a companion of Heraclius, was a bishop over the Christians of Shām. He related that when Heraclius came to Īliyāʾ, he woke one morning troubled in spirit. Some of his patricians said: “We find your appearance strange.” Ibn an-Nāṭūr said: Heraclius was a soothsayer who looked into the stars. He told them when they asked him: “Tonight, when I looked into the stars, I saw that the king of the circumcised has appeared. Who among this people practise circumcision?” They said: “None practise circumcision except the Jews, so do not let their matter trouble you. Write to the cities of your kingdom that they should kill the Jews among them.” While they were in this discussion, a man was brought to Heraclius whom the king of Ghassān had sent to convey news of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When Heraclius had questioned him, he said: “Go and see whether he is circumcised or not.” They looked at him and told him that he was circumcised. He asked him about the Arabs, and he said: “They practise circumcision.” Heraclius said: “This is the king of this nation; he has appeared.” Then Heraclius wrote to a companion of his in Rome who was his equal in knowledge, and Heraclius set out for Ḥimṣ. He had not left Ḥimṣ before a letter came from his companion agreeing with Heraclius’ view about the appearance of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he is a prophet. Heraclius then admitted the great men of the Romans into a palace of his in Ḥimṣ and ordered its doors to be locked. Then he came out and said: “O assembly of Romans, do you wish for success and right guidance, and that your kingdom remain firm? Then pledge allegiance to this prophet.” They bolted like wild asses towards the doors and found them locked. When Heraclius saw their aversion and despaired of their faith, he said: “Bring them back to me.” He said: “I said what I said only to test the firmness of your attachment to your religion, and I have seen it.” So they prostrated before him and were pleased with him. That was the last of Heraclius’ affair. Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, Yūnus and Maʿmar narrated it from az-Zuhrī.
7.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: the report relates Heraclius’ questions to Abū Sufyān and the letter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The closing account of Ibn an-Nāṭūr belongs to the same wording in this edition. No page number from Fatḥ al-Bārī is invented.
